question: Your system extracts invoice data into a JSON schema that has a single total field, and a downstream accounting system consumes the output. Reviewers find that some source invoices print a total that differs from the sum of their own line items. In these cases the extraction sometimes reports the printed total and sometimes silently reports the recomputed sum. Which design change best lets the system catch and surface these discrepancies?

options.text: Run a validation check that compares the total with the line item sum, and retry with the specific error until the model returns values that agree with each other.
options.reason: The conflict is in the source document itself, not a format or structural error. The guide says retries succeed on format and structural errors, not on problems that come from the source content. Forcing agreement pushes the model to alter values instead of flagging the conflict.

options.text: Make the total field nullable and instruct the model to return null whenever the printed total and the line items disagree in the invoice.
options.reason: The guide uses nullable fields for information that is absent from the source. Here both values are present, so returning null discards data instead of flagging the conflict with a conflict_detected boolean.

options.text: Extract a stated_total as printed and a calculated_total summed from the extracted line items, and set a conflict_detected boolean when the two values differ.
options.reason: The guide describes this self-correction validation flow. Extracting calculated_total alongside stated_total flags discrepancies, and a conflict_detected boolean marks inconsistent source data.

options.text: Instruct the model to always replace the printed total with the sum of the extracted line items, so that the single total field stays internally consistent.
options.reason: This hides the inconsistency in the source document instead of flagging it. The guide recommends keeping stated_total and calculated_total side by side so that discrepancies are detected.
